member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.ChatMessage
member.summary:
v61: a chat line a game mode sends (, ) or hands back in place of a player's (). Either or holds the words; when both do, the spans win and the text is ignored. At most 16 spans and 512 characters in all: a message over either is refused, never cut. The plain text every line carries (what the native chat draws, what a bot reads) is the spans' words one after the other. A string converts to a message of that text.
v68: or a and its - the web chat lays the line out with one of the web interface's [theme.chat.templates], a few values filling its {0} to {15}. When the message has no text and no spans of its own, the plain line is the template filled in (the server does it, from the interface in force) - or the params one after the other, with a space between, when it has no such template.

member.name: F:KcdMp.Api.ChatMessage.DefaultColor
member.summary: The colour of a line that names none: white, as a player's own lines are.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.ChatMessage.Text
member.summary: The words, in one colour.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.ChatMessage.Spans
member.summary: The words in pieces of their own styles; when set (and not empty) is ignored.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.ChatMessage.Template
member.summary: v68: the name of a template of the web interface's [theme.chat.templates] (ui.toml) the web chat draws the line with: "ooc", "me", "shout" ... - lower-case letters, digits and _, starting with a letter, 32 characters at most; null or empty = none. The server does not check that the interface has it (a chat that does not draws the plain line). The line carries it as it is, with ; a message with params needs one.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.ChatMessage.Params
member.summary: v68: the values the template's {0} to {15} stand for, each a piece of text (at most 16 of them, 256 characters each, 1024 in all) - always drawn as text, whatever it holds. A message over a cap is refused, never cut.

A line to one player goes to them whatever the channel's visibility; a line to everyone goes to the players the channel is visible to.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.IDatabase
member.summary:
The game mode's own database (2026-09-22): the one opt-in of server.toml, [gamemode.database], a MySQL / MariaDB or PostgreSQL server the mode keeps its accounts, factions, scores and rules in. hands it out, null when the owner configured none. The server's own state (doors, chests, bans) lives apart and is never reachable through this.
Parameters only: @name in the SQL, the values in the dictionary (string, long / int, double, bool, null; a DateTime travels as ISO 8601 text). There is no escape function on purpose: never concatenate a value into the SQL text. A NULL column comes back as null. Integers come back as long, floating numbers as double, dates as ISO 8601 strings.
The async members run the query on a pool thread and are safe to await from any thread; nothing else of the API may be touched off the simulation thread, so continue through . The synchronous members are allowed during only (the config tables loaded before the first player) and throw anywhere else: a slow database must never freeze the tick. Every call is bounded by the config's timeout_seconds and max_rows; a query over slow_query_ms gets a log line. A failing query throws (the Task faults); the server goes on.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerText(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String)
member.summary: A plain chat line (never a "/" command); return false to swallow it (filters, channels). The text is cleaned by the server first: no control, invisible or direction-changing characters, one kind of space, at most three combining marks after a letter, at most 256 characters. A player sending faster than two lines a second after a burst of five, or the same line twice within five seconds, is refused before this is called.

member.summary: v61: a plain chat line with the channel it was typed in ("" = the default one; a name made, checked: the player may see and write into it). What the server calls, after the cleaning and the flood floors. Answers , or a rewrite of the words or of the whole message (, ). The default hands the line to (false = suppress), so a mode that has only that one keeps working.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerCommand(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: A chat line that starts with "/": is the word after the slash (as typed), the rest. Return true when the mode answered it; false lets the server's built-in commands answer ([commands] in server.toml: /give, /item, /tp, /horse, /time ... - the mode wins over any of them by handling the name), then "Unknown command". /fight and /peace are the server's before the mode sees them; a command the mode registered (IServerApi.RegisterCommand) is run before this is asked.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerKeyBinding(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v61: the player pressed ( true) or let go of a key the mode declared (), on whichever physical key they bound to it. At most 20 presses a second from a player (a release is never dropped: every press the mode heard is followed by its release); the name is always a registered one. A held key is reported down once and up once (its repeats are not sent); only a modified game or a reload between the two can break the pair, so a mode that must not act twice keeps its own state.

member.summary: v73: the horse died - a blow (attacker), IServerApi.SetHorseHealth 0 or its own game (a fall: attacker null). It lies on every screen, its rider is off it, and the body is removed a minute later (IServerApi.DestroyEntity sooner).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerThrown(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Int32,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v62: the player was thrown off the horse they ride - a head hit on a branch or a beam (cause 1), the horse throwing them (2), something else (3: their game threw them and the server could not tell why), or the mode's own IServerApi.ThrowPlayerFromHorse (4). : the game's strong throw. It comes before the OnPlayerDismount of the same fall; the player's game plays the fall and the get-up by itself (the server lets them move faster than a walker for a few seconds meanwhile, IPlayer.IsThrown) and every other screen sees it.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerPullDown(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: v62: (on foot, with the right - IServerApi.SetPlayerPullDown) asks to pull off the horse they ride: the server has checked the ask (the weapon's reach and the horse's pace - the game's own numbers (a sword 2.5 m and 6 m/s, a longsword 3 and 7, a halberd 4 and 8, bare hands 2 and 4) plus 1.5 m and 1 m/s, since the positions it has are a few frames old - and pvp, teams, parties, no wall between the two, both players idle) and asks the mode last. Returns the chance the pull succeeds: 1 (the default) always, 0 never (the pair plays, the rider stays in the saddle), a number between them a roll the server makes; a negative number refuses the pull-down altogether (nothing plays). The mode does its own bookkeeping here (a cooldown, protection) - a later refusal of the server's own does not call this again, and the chance taken is the pull-down that then starts.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerPulledDown(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v62: a pull-down is over for : with the game's take-down threw them off the horse (this comes before the OnPlayerDismount of the same fall), without it the pull failed and they are still in the saddle (told at the end of the pair's animation, about 4.5 s after the start). Not called when the pull-down was cut short (a death, a disconnect, a teleport) before its outcome showed, nor for a pull that was to land when the rider's game never took them out of the saddle (a game that failed to play it): a mode that sets state at OnPlayerPullDown lets it expire by time instead of waiting for this.

False refuses (the grab does not start - the carrier is told so); is the player a corpse was (null for anyone else, or a player who left). Not called for the mode's own orders (CarryPlayer, CarryEntity).

Not called for a carry an NPC actor makes.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerPutDownCarryItem(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String,System.Numerics.Vector3)

False refuses (the thief is told so); the mode does its own bookkeeping here - a later refusal of the server's own does not call this again.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerPickpocketEnd(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: v62: a pickpocket session is over. : "took" (stacks moved - of them), "nothing" (the minigame ended with nothing taken, or all of it was vetoed or gone), "caught" (the game's own roll caught the thief; nothing moves - the mode decides the consequence) or "cancelled" (the session was broken off, nothing taken). says why: for the game's own outcomes "succeeded", "detected", "seen", "interrupted", "lost" or "nothing stolen"; for a cancelled one "broken off" (the thief's game), "thief died", "victim died", "thief left", "victim left", "respawned", "moved" (the server moved one of them), "moved away", "mounted", "cart", "flying", "knocked out", "carried", "busy", "fight", "timeout", "victim gone" (an actor removed), "world" (another virtual world), "too fast", "bad claim" or the mode's own word (IServerApi.CancelPickpocket). A reload ends sessions without a word to the mode.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnSiegeImpact(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,System.String,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String)

A mode can do more with it: open a gate struck often enough, switch a layer, count the hits on a wall.

A knocked-down siege ladder comes here too: for each climber it threw off as they come down (the higher they were, the more), then for whoever it lands on - `shooter` is who knocked it down.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerUseItem(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Single,System.String)
member.summary: The player's game used an item (a potion drunk, food eaten, an ointment applied; v23 - and since v76 a book read, a letter or a map opened, a recipe learned, with health 0 and no buff). For a consumable the server is about to apply the tables' effect - the health benefit to its own vitals and the item's buff (GivePlayerBuff); false cancels both (the item is gone from the player's inventory either way - their game consumed it). v76: for a class the mode judges first (IServerApi.SetItemUseCheck) this comes before the game uses the item, and false refuses the use itself - the item stays, nothing is read or eaten.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerUseItem(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Single,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: v76: with the used item's tag id (IServerApi.GivePlayerTaggedItem: the letter that was read), "" for an untagged item. The server calls this one; by default it asks the four-argument one.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerCraft(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: v76: the player started a crafting station - `station` is "alchemy" (the alchemy table), "smithing" (the anvil) or "sharpening" (the grindstone; `itemClass` is the weapon chosen for it, "" for the others). For a station the mode judges first (IServerApi.SetCraftCheck) this comes before it starts and false keeps it from starting - nothing is used; otherwise it comes after the start and the answer changes nothing. What the station makes reaches as the game's own "craft" ("unmapped" for the anvil's work).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerItemWear(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: v76: the game wore one of the player's own items (a blow, a block, a shot) or mended it (a smith, a whetstone, a repair kit) by at least a whole percent: its condition went from `before` to `after` (0..100, the percent the game's inventory shows). Return null to let it be, or the condition it should have instead - `before` keeps it as it was (no wear here), any other number sets it; their game is set to it. An item's arrival (a pickup, a chest, a grant) and the mode's own SetPlayerItemHealth are no wear and do not come here. A repair kit's repair comes twice: the repaired item's mend and the kit's own loss (a kit's charge is its condition, category "Ointment") - keep both at `before` to undo a repair.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerInventoryChange(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: v53: what the player carries or their purse changed, by their client's report (within about a second of the change; the audit has judged it already) - the moment to save it (IServerApi.GetPlayerInventory, GetPlayerMoney). An item given to a chest, the ground or a shop is the server's at once; saving the player here keeps the two in step. Not for their horse's saddlebags (OnHorseItemsChange).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnClientEvent(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The player's client sent a script event (its Lua's SendServerEvent(name, payload)): the client half of a mode's own feature talks to the server half here. At most 30 a second and 4 KB each per client; the payload is whatever string the client sent, trusted no further than any other input.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnClientEvent(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The same event with where it came from: is "lua" for a client script's SendServerEvent and the frame's name for an event a page of the mode's web interface emitted. The word is the client's own - a game that was changed can put either one on any event - so it says which twin of a screen spoke, never who may do what. The server calls this one; the default hands the event to the three-argument , so a mode that has only that one keeps working. A client sends 30 events a second at most and 64 KB a second in all, scripts' and pages' together; a script's event holds 4 KB at most, a page's 16 KB.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerWebStatus(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The player's web layer (the engine that draws the mode's web interface) changed state, and once right after with the state the client reported when it joined (nothing when it reported none): is "off" (no web layer, or the player turned the servers' interfaces off), "starting", "ready" or "failed"; is the client's short word for it, cleaned. A mode that draws a screen on the web and on its Lua twin decides which to open here.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerWebReady(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String)
member.summary: A page of the web interface (a frame) is loaded and listening: sent again each time the frame is loaded anew and each time a hidden frame that is ready is shown again ( on it).
member.remarks: Hiding the frame and showing it again from inside this callback would call it again: a loop, held back to a few a second by the server (the frame is ready at once, and a call that waited is never lost).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerWebError(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: A page reported a script error. Only with [client] ui_report_errors = true, at most 5 a minute for each player; the texts are the client's word, cleaned and cut short. is the script's file in the interface, its line (0 = unknown).

member.summary: v83: the player's copy of a web surface's page is ready (IServerApi.CreateWebSurface) - when the surface came within the page's range of them, and again after every reload of it. Send that copy what it should show (IServerApi.SendPlayerWebSurfaceMessage): a copy that was out of range missed the messages before.

The picked spot is gone for everyone until it grows back. The item of a pick no longer comes to OnPlayerTakeWorldItem.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerAuditViolation(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: The item ledger (v62; the inventory audit of v16 before it) found the player holding `amount` of an item class - what their client reports - where the server's records credit `allowed` (what it bound to the player plus the gives still on their way), and is about to remove the excess from their game. A single unexplained item is removed, never a kick: a player is kicked only for cheating proven beyond doubt (OnPlayerCheatDetected, [audit] action). The purse is the game's money item, counted in tenths of a Groschen. Return false to vouch for it (the records take the amount); true lets the removal happen (in observe mode - [audit] mode - it is only logged).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerAuditViolation(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.String)
member.summary: The same, with where the items the records do not explain came from (2026-10-11): `origins` is a comma-separated list such as "native unmapped", "unknown" (nothing of the game's own the client watches made it - an edited count, or a way the client does not see), "native craft", "foreign_inv" (moved in from an inventory the client does not track), "outfit" or "pickup" - empty when none is known. The server calls this one; by default it answers what the four-argument one answers, so a mode that overrides only that one keeps working.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerNativeItem(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: v62: the player's game made an item of its own - a craft, a butchering, a herb picked, a loot, the dice, a tool, a bite that leaves a vial, a smith's work, a script of the game - and the server has no record that explains it. `kind` names the producer: "craft", "butcher", "herb", "loot", "dice", "tool", "eat", "wear", "smith", "script", "setitems", "unmapped", "foreign_inv". Return true to adopt it (the records take it, as if the server had given it), false to have it removed, or null (the default) to leave it to the server's rule - the producers the game has in multiplayer are accepted for ordinary items within a value budget, and refused for guarded classes (weapons, armour, ammunition, money: [audit] guarded_categories) until a mode adopts them here. "smith" (2026-10-06) is what the player forged at an anvil - a class one of the game's smithing recipes makes, inside the smithing session the server saw start, with that recipe's materials gone from the bag in the session: accepted, guarded or not, two pieces a minute at most, unless the mode returns false.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerCheatDetected(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Boolean,System.String)
member.summary: v62: the server's measures or the player's own client found a sign of cheating - `kind` is "speed", "blink", "noclip", "jump", "fall", "horse", "never_hit", "void_ratio", "code", "integrity", "timescale", "clock", "state", "foreign_call", "inventory_overflow", "save_reenabled", "loot_flags", the ledger's own ("ledger_desync", "ledger_silent", "removal_ignored", "removal_refused", "forged_claim" ...) and the kinds of the progression, nourishment / energy and carry-weight checks: PROVEN "progress_write_repeat" (a game that writes the same forged XP, level or perk points back after the server put them back, three times within ten minutes, each time a rise of at least 25 XP, or of 2 or more perk points or a perk) and "vitals_write_repeat" (the same for a nourishment or energy that is frozen); ADVISORY "progress" (a rise of XP, a level, perk points or a perk that nothing explains), "progress_ack" (the game does not confirm the server's orders), "progress_gate" (the game's own XP counting is not running, so its awards cannot be seen), "vitals" (a nourishment or energy held over the game's maximum, or a maximum the game reports that is not the game's), "vitals_rewrite" (a value written back to its maximum and written up again, short of proof), "weight" (sprinting or mounting while carrying more than the game allows, a capacity above what the strength allows, a horse's saddlebags over their limit) and "code_guarded" (an edit of the game's code inside a function these checks rely on). Of the weight hints only the capacity above what the strength, perks, potions and drinks allow reaches the mode; the others and the hints about a nourishment or energy that falls too slowly or rises with no meal wait for their measurements: they are counted and logged and not told to the mode yet. `proven` is true for what the server holds against the client beyond doubt - [audit] action (log, kick or ban) follows it - and false for a signal that can be wrong (a measure against a modded server's speeds, an overlay, a lag burst): those are only counted and logged, and what they mean is the mode's to decide - it may kick, freeze or flag the player through the API. The advisory kinds of the progression, nourishment / energy and weight checks and "code_guarded" are evidence for a mode's own rule, never a reason to kick by themselves: the server tells the mode (and its log) of one at most every 10 seconds and 30 times an hour per player and kind, however often it finds it. A proven one is never held back. Return false to tolerate a proven one: the [audit] action does not happen for this event. `detail` is a line for the log.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerCheatDetected(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Boolean,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: 2026-10-07: with `count` - how many of this kind the player raised this session, this one included. The kinds a moving player can raise with every report ("speed", "blink", "noclip", "jump", "fall", "horse") and the floods ("ledger_flood", "foreign_call", "loot_flags") reach the mode five times a session, then once every 5 seconds per kind - the count says how many came in between. A proven one always reaches it. The server calls this one; by default it asks the four-argument one.

Return true to take it: the server applies it as IServerApi.SetPlayerLook does (every screen, the player's own too) - the place to save it. The default refuses, so a mode that offers no look of its own takes none.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnDiceMatchStart(KcdMp.Api.IDiceMatch)

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnDiceMatchEnd(KcdMp.Api.IDiceMatch,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String)
member.summary: v54: a dice match ended - `winner` reached the goal ("goal"), or the other gave up ("gave up"), let a move time out ("timeout"), left the server ("left") or died ("died"); or it was called off (winner null: "out of step" - the two games parted ways, "failed" - a game could not start it, "the mode", "a fight", "walked away"). The stakes have moved already: the winner holds both, a call-off gave each theirs back. A leaving player is still a player here.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerGainXP(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String,System.Single)
member.summary: v61: the player's game awarded them XP on its own (a kill, a hit, a distance walked, a book read) and made it wait for this word. is "stat" or "skill", the lower-case name, the award times the XP rate (; a rate of 0 asks nothing). Return the XP to give: the same number lets it through, a smaller or larger one scales it, 0 or less refuses it, null gives . XP the mode gives itself () does not come here.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.WantsXpGains
member.summary: v61: whether the mode judges every XP award of the game in . The players' games hold each award for the server's word only when this is true (a Lua mode: when it defines OnPlayerGainXP); otherwise the rate alone decides, on the spot.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerLevelUp(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: v61: the player's game reported a stat or skill level higher than the server had - a level the player earned (kind "stat" or "skill", the lower-case name, the new level). Not for a level the mode set itself (): only for a rise over the record. The player's main level comes here too, as the stat "mainlevel": the level the game shows for them, which rises when their stats and skills do. The game derives it from those, so a rise the mode's own sets (a character restore, a , the [spawn] stat_level floor) cause a few seconds later is not told.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerProgressChange(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v61: the progression of record changed by the player's report: is true when a level or a perk did (worth saving now), false when only XP or the soul's states (nourishment, energy) moved (save on a timer). The first whole report of a session counts as a change of levels. Not for the mode's own sets (, ...).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerOutfitChange(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: v82: the player's outfits changed (): they put an outfit together, changed what one wears or switched to another, and their game reported it. The mode's moment to save them with the character. Not for the mode's own ; the report that answers it comes a moment later.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerProgressViolation(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: v62: the progression check found a rise of the player's soul the server cannot explain - XP, a level, perk points or a perk - and is about to put it back ([audit] mode = "enforce", for a rule that acts) or has logged that it would (observe: the call comes all the same, and nothing is sent to the player's game). is "xp" (a stat's or skill's XP), "level", "points" (unspent perk points), "perk" (a perk bought without points or below its level) or "baseline" (a fresh game above what a fresh character holds). is the lower-case stat, skill or perk name, what the soul says (for "xp" and "level" the XP counted over every level together, for "points" the points, for a perk below its level the level it asks, 1 for a perk bought without points) and what the server can explain (the level it explains for a perk below its level). Under enforce this version acts on a clear XP or level rise (300 XP or more that nothing explains, over three times what the server explains or three levels above it; never with story quests on), on points and on both kinds of perk; a smaller rise is only logged. 's GateDown with a large excess is a trainer's mark the mode may act on itself. Return false to vouch for it: the server takes the reported value as the player's progress - a custom teacher, an event's reward, a story server's quest XP. True, the default, lets the set-back happen. At most 8 calls per burst and 30 a minute per player, then the set-back goes ahead without asking. Where a rule acts, the record reads is the server's own figure, so a value that was put back is never the one a mode saves. A server with story quests on that enforces must vouch for them here: the story's quests, teachers and scripts give XP and levels the server cannot see being earned, and it treats them like any other unexplained rise.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IGameMode.OnPlayerDiscoveryChange(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.DiscoveryKinds,System.String)
member.summary: v65: the record of what the player discovered grew - their game reported more of this kind than the record held (a place found, a book read or studied further), or it reported a kind for the first time, which is also the sign that now holds the game's own state (a mode that restores a character waits for that before it trusts what it reads). The moment to save: it runs at most once per kind every five seconds, from the tick, so a walk across the map is a few calls, not hundreds. is the level of the record, empty for the reading kind (global). Not for the mode's own sets (). A change still waiting for its window when the player leaves is told at once, just before (and when the mode is shut down or replaced), so a mode that saves what it was told never misses what a player found in their last seconds.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.IParty
member.summary: A party (v38): two or more players grouped by an accepted invitation or by the mode. The server keeps the record, the invitations and the frames on the members' screens; the mode writes every command and rule around and the party callbacks of . Ids count up from 1 and are never reused during a server run. A party ends when it falls to one member (the last one leaves too) or when the mode disbands it. Members cannot hurt each other unless the server's [party] friendly_fire says so.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer
member.summary: A connected player as a game mode sees it: identity, the server's record of where they are (metres, CryEngine yaw: 0 = facing +Y, counter-clockwise) and a bag for script-owned data. Instances live from the handshake to the disconnect; keep the , not the object, across ticks if in doubt ( answers null once they are gone).

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.Uid
member.summary: 2026-10-07: the player's id on this server - 32 lowercase hex, the same at every join from the same game install, "" when their game sent none (an older launcher, a direct join without the launcher's query). Made from a secret only their install holds, so another player's game cannot claim it; a player's ids on two servers have nothing in common. A key for the mode's own records (characters, bans, ranks) where a password would otherwise be asked; a reinstall of Windows or a wiped app-data folder gives a new one.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.Inventory
member.summary: What the player carries as the server's item records hold it (IServerApi.GetPlayerInventory is the same list): one stack per class, and each piece they wear alone with Worn set. It is what the server accepted as theirs - the spawn outfit, its own gives, pickups it placed, takes it validated - plus the mode's gives still on their way, less the takes on theirs, so a give of the mode's shows at once and an item a cheat tool conjured is not in it under [audit] mode = "enforce" (under "observe" it is what their game holds). member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.AuditViolations
member.summary: How many times the item check took unexplained items out of the player's game this session ([audit] in server.toml): one for each excess ordered out whatever the number of items in it, plus the removals for a pickup or a take the server itself refused (under "observe" only those count; what observe would remove is in the log). Not a count of cheats - a removal is the check working, and an honest player whose game and the server disagree for a moment gets one; a cheat the server can prove is IGameMode.OnPlayerCheatDetected's.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.IsThrown
member.summary: v64: the player has just been thrown off their horse and is still falling, lying or getting up (a head hit, the horse, the mode's IServerApi.ThrowPlayerFromHorse): a few seconds from the throw - the same span the server lets them fall faster than a walker may move. member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.RiderHeadHit

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.RiderThrow
member.summary: v64: a head hit, the horse or IServerApi.ThrowPlayerFromHorse may throw this rider (true unless a mode called IServerApi.SetPlayerRiderThrow(false)). A pull-down is not a throw and does not read this.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.CanPullDown

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.IsInPullDown
member.summary: v64: this player is in a pull-down - pulling a rider off a horse or being pulled off one: from the start of the game's take-down pair until a couple of seconds after its end (the span the server lets the two bodies move as the pair does). False otherwise.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.IsCarrying
member.summary: v64: the player carries a body or another player over their shoulder (a grab they made while IServerApi.SetCarrying allowed it, or the mode's CarryPlayer / CarryEntity), from the start of the grab to the end of the put-down. While they do, they cannot fight, ride, take a cart seat, make an emote or start a dice match, and the server holds their pace to the carry's (a quarter above the speed the carry was given).

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.IsCarried
member.summary: v64: a player or an NPC actor carries this player (their screen shows them knocked out meanwhile, and the carrier's body carries them on every screen). While they are carried the server does not judge their position - it is the carrier's - and they cannot fight or act.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.IsKnockedOut
member.summary: v64: the player is knocked out (IServerApi.SetPlayerKnockedOut): the game's own knock-out - down, the eyes shut - until the timer runs out or the mode wakes them. A knocked-out player can be carried and cannot fight, act, ride, make an emote or start a dice match.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.IsPickpocketable

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IPlayer.CanPickpocket

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerInvisible(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean)
member.summary: 2026-10-09: the player invisible to every other player (an admin who watches unseen) - or seen again. Nothing of them shows on another screen: no body, no clothes, no nameplate, no horse they ride, nothing in their hands; their voice is not heard and their party's compass has no blip for them. Their own game is untouched (they see and hear everyone), server animals leave them be, a carry they are part of ends and no player may carry them or be carried by them meanwhile. Their roster entry, chat and commands stay: what else to hide is the mode's (combine with SetPlayerFlying, SetPlayerVoiceMuted ...). Per viewer: . Runtime only: a reload of the mode shows everyone again.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SendClientEvent(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: A named event with a string payload to the player's client, where the client Lua's OnServerEvent(name, payload) receives it — the server half of a mode's own feature talks to its client half here (the other direction is IGameMode.OnClientEvent). The name is at most 64 bytes of UTF-8 and the payload at most 60000: a bigger one is refused (logged, never cut - a cut payload is broken JSON) and nothing is sent. The names that start with kcdmp: are the engine's own and refused the same way. The event reaches the client's Lua and every frame of the mode's web interface whose ui.toml lets it receive the name (by default the names that start with the frame's own name and a dot). These two return nothing and never throw for it; says whether it went.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.TrySendClientEvent(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String)
member.summary: that says whether the event was sent: false when the name is over 64 bytes or starts with kcdmp:, or the payload is over 60000 bytes of UTF-8 (refused and logged, nothing sent).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.TrySendClientEventToAll(System.String,System.String)
member.summary: The same for every player past the handshake (): false when the event was refused for its size.

Fire and forget: a late arrival sees nothing, a looping effect plays until the level unloads. dir is the effect's up (0 0 1 = straight up); scale 1 = as authored. Returns how many players got it (0 for an empty name; a name the game does not know only warns in the clients' logs).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetZoneHittable(KcdMp.Api.IZone,System.Boolean)
member.summary: 2026-10-03: the zone catches what reaches it - every arrow, bolt or ball a player shoots whose flight enters it (IGameMode.OnProjectileHitZone; the server flies the shot itself from the shooter's report and stops it at the ground, at the level's walls when the collision export is loaded, and at the body it struck) and every swing whose reach does (IGameMode.OnMeleeHitZone). The zone is invisible and stops nothing: a shot flies on through it and may enter another.

member.summary: Bans the player's name and address for a while (seconds; 0 = for good) and kicks them: a Hello under the name or from the address is refused with the reason until then. Bans are kept in the server's own database (data/server.db) and survive a restart.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.Unban(System.String)

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsBanned(System.String)

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ReloadGameMode(System.String)
member.summary: Reloads the game mode at the end of the tick (v24): the running mode is shut down, its zones, HUD texts, props, state bags, nameplates, colors, teams and timers are torn down, the script (or the plugin) is loaded again from [gamemode] script and told about every player again; the players and the world's other things stay. A script that fails to load leaves the built-in freeroam in charge. /reload (admins) and [gamemode] watch (a changed file) do the same.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GameModeFolder
member.summary: The full path of the folder the game mode's file lies in ([gamemode] script), "" for the built-in freeroam (2026-10-03). A plugin is read into memory so a rebuild may overwrite it while the server runs: its Assembly.Location is empty, and files it keeps beside itself are found from here.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.Post(System.Action)
member.summary: Runs on the simulation thread at the start of the next tick, before the mode's , in posting order. The one member a plugin may call from any thread: slow work (a database, a web request) runs on a task of the plugin's own and posts its result back here, where the rest of the API is legal again. A posted action is a callback of the mode like any other (its exception is the mode's); what is still queued when the mode is reloaded is dropped with the mode that posted it.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.Database
member.summary: The game mode's own database (2026-09-22): server.toml [gamemode.database], MySQL / MariaDB or PostgreSQL, null when the owner configured none (a mode says so and runs without). The server's own state is not in it and not reachable through it. See for the rules: parameters only, async off the tick, the sync calls during OnInit alone.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GlobalState
member.summary: The state bags (v20): string keys and values the server sets and every client's Lua reads (GetGlobalState(key), GetPlayerState(pid, key), GetEntityState(id, key), and OnStateChange(scope, id, key, value) on each change) - the way a mode's client half learns a team, a round, a flag carrier or a marker without a script event per client. The global and the players' bags reach every client from its join on; an entity's follows its Spawn to whoever sees it. A null value removes the key. Not persisted; a player's bag goes with the session, an entity's with the entity. Limits: a key of 1-48 characters, a value of at most StateValueMax bytes, StateKeysMax keys per bag (a set beyond them is refused and logged).

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.Doors
member.summary: The level's doors and containers (v15), in sync on every client whatever the mode: a door's state of record once anyone touched it (key = the entity's level name, e.g. "AnimDoor[Door/door_village_left32_77d417c2-...]"), a container's contents once anyone opened it (v39: rolled from the game's own loot tables the first time, or empty - [containers] loot). Where a level gives one name to several containers or item slots (Stash96 five times in kutnohorsko), one keeps the name as its key and each other one is the name with its place in whole metres, "Stash96@3160,787,57". Untouched objects are the level's defaults. Doors, chests and taken items survive a restart (world.json beside the player records).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetDoorPosition(System.String)
member.summary: Where the level's objects stand (2026-09-22, from the tables export: every door, chest and takeable item slot with its place; null / -1 for a key the export does not know or a level without one). Metres in the level's space. The nearest-object functions answer "the door the player stands at" within the radius (0 = no limit): a mode's command on the nearest chest, a rule set by standing next to it, with no key in sight. /objectinfo shows the keys in the game.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.LevelDoors
member.summary: v57: every door of the level in the tables export, touched or not (the keys GetDoorPosition answers for) - where a mode finds the level's houses and settlements: a street to put someone in, a village to spread people over. Empty without the export. lists only those anyone touched.

False for an empty or too long key, or past 512 doors or (v85) about 60 KB of keys with the SetDoorPrompt rows. v85: the changes go out once, at the end of the tick, only what changed.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsDoorChecked(System.String)

False for another word, an empty or too long key, or past 512 doors.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetDoorLockSides(System.String)

member.summary: v95: switches the level's herbs of a kind ("*" every kind) off (enabled = false) or on again: within `radius` metres of a point on the map, or on the whole level with a radius of 0. Switching on takes away every zone of the kind whose middle lies within the radius of the point (radius 0: every zone of the kind). At most 256 zones; a newcomer gets them at the spawn. Not kept across a restart.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.HerbZones

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.Gates
member.summary: v41: the level's gates - the animated defensive pieces (a portcullis that drops, a drawbridge that lifts), the server's alone: the game gives players no hand on them, so a mode (or /gate) starts every cycle and every client plays it from the server's clock. The keys are the entities' level names; the retail levels have two, both in kutnohorsko. A gate starts a server run at the level's default (open = passable) and its state survives a restart with the doors. v59: two more of the kind "gate" - "malesov_courtyard_gate" (kutnohorsko, the Malesov double gate barred by a latch) and "trosky_south_gate" (trosecko, the door in Trosky castle's south gate) - are two of the level's story layers each, so they are at the other end at once (no cycle; ); they start a server run open like the other two (the story starts them shut), so a mode that wants one shut says so. Three more of that kind since 2026-10-03: "raborsch_gate" and "ruthard_palace_gate" (kutnohorsko, the gates of Raborsch fortress and of Ruthard Palace in Kuttenberg) and "nebakov_gate" (trosecko, the gate of Nebakov fortress).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetGateState(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v41: starts a cycle towards open (passable) or closed; a moving gate turns back from where it is. Refused when it is there or heading there already.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ToggleGate(System.String)
member.summary: v41: heads the gate away from the end it is at, reversing one already moving.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.NearestGate(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: v41: the key of the gate nearest the point within the radius (metres), null when none.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetLevelLayer(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v59: switches one of the level's story layers on or off on every client, at once - the parts of the level the single-player quests show and hide as the story goes (a gate shut or open, a wall whole or broken), its scenery and its entities together. The name is the layer's full name as the level lists it (letters, digits, '_' and '-', with its GUID: "gate_open_a12b1f05-20f2-4d96-825c-57aea7eec798"). A newcomer gets every layer switched so far; a name the level lacks changes nothing (the client logs it). Refused for a name no layer could have, or one already switched that way. Not kept across a restart: switch the layers again when the mode starts.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetLevelLayer(System.String)

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CreateQuest(KcdMp.Api.QuestDefinition,System.String@)
member.summary: v81: a quest in the game's own journal - the mode defines it once (its name, description, kind and objectives, each with its diary lines and an optional marker), then gives it to players and moves each player's progress: the journal's lists and diary, the HUD's "quest started" / objective banners and the lettered markers on the compass and the world map are the game's own. Null when the definition is refused (reason says why), its key is another quest's, or the 1024 quests are used up. The server keeps a player's quests for their session only: a mode that keeps them across visits stores by each quest's key (an id lasts one server run) and gives them back with and at the next login.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.LevelLayersNear(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: v77: the level's story layers with a solid piece (a wall, a fence, a door, a heap) within the radius of a point, the nearest first - how a mode (or an admin with /layer near) finds the layer of something it wants gone or back. Needs a tables export of 2026-10-06 or later (the layers' pieces); empty with an older one. Layers of more than 4000 pieces (the level's own ground layers) are not listed. When a layer is switched off, the server's own collision leaves its pieces out too.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetLevelBarriers(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v77: lifts (on = false) or puts back (on = true) the level's own invisible barriers in an area on every client - the walls no one sees that stop a player at deep water ("you cannot swim"), at the level's edge and along some story paths, so players can wade a moat to a ladder. An area is a circle on the map (x, y, radius in metres, 0.1 to 500); a barrier piece that reaches into it is lifted whole. Lifting at a place already lifted (its middle within 1 m) changes its radius; putting back takes away every lifted area whose middle lies within the radius of the point. At most 64 areas; a newcomer gets them all at the spawn. Not kept across a restart: lift them again when the mode starts.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.LevelBarrierAreas
member.summary: v77: the areas where the level's barriers are lifted, in the order they were lifted.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.WorldSeconds
member.summary: v39: the world clock the restock timers run on - world seconds since this world's first start ([world] time_ratio per real second).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPlayerInventory(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: The player's whole inventory as the server's item records hold it (IPlayer.Inventory): what the server accepted as theirs plus the mode's gives still on their way, less the takes on theirs - so a GivePlayerItem or SetPlayerInventory of the mode's shows at once, and an item a cheat tool conjured is not in it under [audit] mode = "enforce" (under "observe" it is what their game holds). v53's Worn is set on one item per piece they wear (IPlayer.Equipment; a stack of a worn class is split into the worn one and the rest). v76: Health is each item's condition, 0..100 - one stack per class and condition, a worn piece's its own. The money is not in it (IPlayer.Money); empty until their items are known, a moment after the spawn.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerInventory(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{KcdMp.Api.ContainerItem})
member.summary: v53: the player's inventory made exactly these items (a class by any catalogue key; the money stays - GivePlayerMoney): compared with what the server's records hold, the gives and takes still on their way counted, what they hold beyond the list is taken (an exact order their game carries out), what they miss is given (the server's record from this moment, the game makes it a moment later). Called again before the first call's orders are done, it orders nothing twice. An item with Worn is put on (given first when they miss it); nothing is taken off - what they wear and keep stays on. v76: Health is the item's condition, 0..100 (100 = new): a missing item is made at it, one they hold is set to it.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.EmptyPlayerInventory(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v53: every item the player holds taken (the money stays); keepWorn leaves what they wear on them.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ShowPlayerDialogue(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Int32,System.String,System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{KcdMp.Api.DialogueOption},KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String@)

The player's movement is held while it is open; their pick, or their close, comes to with the mode's own `dialogId` (a pick closes the page unless the callback shows the next). With an actor the page closes when the player walks away from it (5 m), or it dies or goes; the speaker's name defaults to the actor's. The usual place to call it is OnPlayerInteractActor on an actor with a Talk prompt (). False with the reason when it cannot (not in the world, dead, no choices, too many ...).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerAdmin(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Makes (or unmakes) the player an admin for this session. Admins are the mode's (2026-09-22): the server keeps no list and no accounts; a mode promotes from its own database, its own file or its own rule, in OnPlayerConnect or after its own login. The flag unlocks the built-in admin commands ([commands]).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetSecretCommand(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Declares a chat command secret (2026-09-22): the clients mask the typing of "/name ..." and keep the line out of their chat history - a mode's own /login and /register. Declared at init; the list is sent to every client and emptied by a reload. The server never echoes or logs a command's argument itself; the mode's own Log lines are the mode's to keep clean.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.HashPassword(System.String)
member.summary: Password hashing for a mode's own accounts (PBKDF2-SHA256, a random salt, 20 000 rounds): store what HashPassword returns as it is (one text) and check a login with VerifyPassword. Never store a password in the clear. The hash costs a few milliseconds on the simulation thread: a login's worth, not a per-tick thing.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerCamera(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: 2026-10-07: the player's view at x y z looking at lookX lookY lookZ (metres) - a cutscene, a view over a town - gliding there from where their view is over `glideMs` milliseconds (0 = a cut, at most 60000), with the field of view `fov` in degrees (10-120; 0 = their own). Their body stays where it is, its head shown, and their keys still move it ( holds them). It holds until ; a rejoin starts with their own view. False before the player joined or for a point that looks nowhere (the same as the camera's).

member.summary: Puts a Ready player into the world (or moves one who already is).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerPos(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Nullable{System.Single})
member.summary: Moves a player who is in the world; a null yaw keeps their heading.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerFlying(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean,System.Single,System.String@)
member.summary: v57: lets the player fly, or lands them. Flying, their client moves them along the view with the movement keys (Space up, C down, Shift three times faster), with no gravity and through walls, and the server's speed, terrain and wall checks and fall damage leave them alone - until a few seconds after the landing, which puts them on the ground under them. is the pace in m/s (1-50; 0 = 12). False, with the reason as the player reads it, when they are not in the world, dead, on horseback or in a cart; a death, a mount, a cart seat and a respawn land them.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerChatVisible(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v60: shows or hides the chat on the player's screen (a login screen, a cutscene). Hidden, none of its lines show and Enter opens no chat box (one open at the moment closes); messages still arrive and show again with the chat. It lasts until changed or the player leaves; each visit starts shown. The player's own setting can hide it as well.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerThirdPerson(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.ThirdPersonMode,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v62: sets the player's third-person view - first person only, the player switches with their third-person key, always third person. It lasts until changed or the player leaves; each visit starts with Off, so a mode that wants the view sets it at the join. The game's own camera still takes over in a dialogue, a menu and a minigame; riding a horse keeps the view, and so do fighting and aiming a bow, a crossbow or a gun unless the mode says otherwise: false puts the player in first person while they fight with a sword, an axe or fists, false while a bow, a crossbow or a gun is drawn (each goes back to third person when the fight or the aiming ends). While a bow, a crossbow or a gun is in the hands in third person an aiming dot shows at the centre of the screen; false keeps it off (first person always keeps the game's own look). Each call sets the whole rule, so leaving the three out keeps third person and the dot on. A setting of KCD:MP's own camera: a camera mod the player runs themselves is not stopped by it.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerInterface(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Sets who draws a component for one player: "native", "hidden" or - for "chat" and "scoreboard" alone - "default" (the game's own web version) or the name of a frame of the web interface in force (any case). False, with the reason, for a player who is not connected ("not connected"), a component that does not exist ("unknown component 'x'"), a component that cannot be hidden ("the shop cannot be hidden"), a web drawer for a component that has none ("the party has no web version yet"), a frame when the server has no web interface ("no interface is loaded") or one that is not among its frames ("no such frame in the interface"), and a frame that already draws another component of the player ("the frame mychat already draws the scoreboard"). A web drawer is the server's wish: the player's game draws the component natively until it can show the web one, and says so (see ). A frame the interface in force loses (a reload, an edit) draws nothing: the component is native until the frame is back, and the ask stands. The "party" drawer is the party frames of : "hidden" is the frames off, and the two calls read each other.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPlayerInterface(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String)
member.summary: The drawer a player has for a component: Requested is what the server asks for (the player's own setting, else the one for everyone, else the web interface's ui.toml, else native - a frame the interface in force does not have is native here) and Effective is what draws it now. They are the same for a native or hidden component; for a web drawer ("default" or a frame) the effective one is the drawer the player's game last reported when it names the one asked for, and native until then and while their game cannot show it (no web layer, a failed engine, a page that is not ready, a renderer that died). The report is the game's word and advice only. Null for a player who is not connected or a component that does not exist. (Lua: two values.)

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetInterfaceForAll(System.String,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: for everyone, and for whoever joins later (until a reload): it replaces what was asked for any one player. For "party" it changes what [party] frames says for newcomers as well. A frame is refused ("the frame mychat already draws the scoreboard") when it already draws another component for the world or for any player.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerInterfaceOptions(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{System.String,System.String},System.String@)
member.summary: Sets options of a component for one player, by key - the chat: anchor (top-left, top, top-right, left, center, right, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right), margin_x 0-960, margin_y 0-540, width 300-1200, lines 4-20, backing_alpha 0-100, backing_alpha_open 0-100, font_scale 0.6-1.6; the scoreboard: mode (hold or toggle), title (at most 64 characters); the party: anchor (top-left, left, bottom-left, top-right, right, bottom-right), margin_x 0-960, margin_y 0-1000, show_stamina; the nameplates: color (RRGGBB), font_scale 0.5-2, bar_width 40-240; the compass: span 30-180; the hud (v61): one switch for each of the game's own HUD pieces (), 1 shown (the default) or 0 hidden - true, false, on, off, yes and no are read as 1 and 0 ( sets one). Sizes are pixels at 1080 rows of screen. False, with the reason, for a player who is not connected, an unknown component or option, or a value out of range ("lines must be a whole number from 4 to 20"); nothing changes then, not even the valid keys of the same call.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetInterfaceOptionsForAll(System.String,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyDictionary{System.String,System.String},System.String@)
member.summary: for everyone, and for whoever joins later (until a reload): the keys given replace what was asked for any one player under those keys.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsPlayerWebReady(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: True when the player's web layer runs: their game said "ready" (and has not said anything else since).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsPlayerWebFrameReady(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String)
member.summary: True when the frame of the web interface reported ready in the player's game and has not reported gone since (a frame that is hidden stays ready).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ShowPlayerWebFrame(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Shows a frame to the player: made if it is not there yet, a hidden one shown again with its page as it was.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.HidePlayerWebFrame(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Hides a frame from the player: it is kept alive but drawn nowhere and holds no focus, its page keeps its state.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.DestroyPlayerWebFrame(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Closes a frame for the player: its page ends and the memory it used is freed (a hidden frame keeps both), it gives up its focus, and the game reports it gone. makes it anew, its page loaded from the start. Closing a frame that is not open does nothing.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerWebFocus(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.String@)
member.summary: Asks for the player's keyboard and / or cursor for the frame (the frame's focus setting decides on their side: "never" refuses, "input" gives the keyboard only after their own click or key in it, "open" gives it at once with the cursor). keeps the game's movement keys while no text field of the page has the focus (it needs the keyboard as well). Neither the keyboard nor the cursor takes the frame's focus away.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerCursor(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean,System.String@)
member.summary: Brings the player's cursor up, or takes it away - the same switch as their cursor key and a client script's SetCursorShown: the game's own pointer, in the world, the clicks going to the web interface under it and to client scripts' OnCursorClick. Needs no web interface. A request made while the player is not in the world (the spawn's own loading screen) is kept until they are, a minute at most; one of the game's menus, a load and the end of the session take the cursor away again, and the player's own key still turns it over. Refused only with "no such player".

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SendPlayerWebMessage(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Object,System.String@)
member.summary: Sends one value to a frame: its page's KcdMp.onMessage gets exactly it, queued until the frame is ready. The value is written as JSON by System.Text.Json: a string becomes a JSON string, a JsonNode or JsonElement is sent as it is, any other object (a number, a boolean, a dictionary, a record) is serialised. Refused with "no data" for null, "too big" over 60000 bytes of UTF-8 JSON and "reserved key" for a JSON object with a __kcdmp key at the top (that key marks the engine's own traffic), and with the reason it has no JSON form for a value that has none.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CreateWebSurface(System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,KcdMp.Api.WebSurfaceOptions)
member.summary: v83: a web surface - a page of the web interface (ui.toml [surfaces.<name>]) drawn on a board in the world, every player's game showing its own copy of it: a notice board, a shop sign, a screen. The board stands at x, y, z (its centre) facing yawDeg (like a prop's yaw: 0 faces +Y), width x height metres (0.1 - 20); the options tilt it, make it glow, give it a use prompt (the use key calls IGameMode.OnPlayerUseWebSurface) and a world. The page fills the board whatever its shape (its pixels are its ui.toml width and height). A player's copy paints while they are within the page's range; the mode hears each copy's ready (IGameMode.OnPlayerWebSurfaceReady) and answers it with what that copy should show. An entity of EntityKind.Surface (DestroyEntity removes it; a reload removes them all). Null for a name the interface does not declare, a size out of bounds or a full world.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetWebSurfacePos(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: v83: a web surface moved and turned (its page carries on as it is). False for anything that is no surface.

member.summary: v83: a web surface's size in metres (0.1 - 20 a side; its page keeps its pixels). False for anything that is no surface or a size out of bounds.

member.summary: v83: how much a surface's page shines by itself, 0 - 1 (see ).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SendWebSurfaceMessage(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Object,System.String@)

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.RegisterUiFallback(System.String,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: A screen a mode has twice, a web frame and a Lua one (a client script's box). From now on and send an event named "<frame>.x" by that name to a player whose web layer starts or runs and whose interface has the frame, and as "<luaEventPrefix>.x" to everyone else - the Lua twin listens to the prefix. The choice is made for each event and each player, so a player whose web layer fails while the screen is open is sent the twin's events with no twin open: close the screen and open it again in ("failed"). The events that come back keep their names. The registry is emptied when the mode is reloaded. Answers false with the reason for a frame name that is not one (lower-case letters, digits and -) and for an empty prefix.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SendChatMessage(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.ChatMessage,System.String@)
member.summary: Sends a player a chat message (: words or styled spans, a channel, a colour, and - v68 - a template of the web interface's chat templates with the params that fill it). Refused - never cut - with "no such player", "no such channel", "too many spans (16 at most)", "the message is over 512 characters", "empty message", and for a template "bad template name (...)", "too many params (16 at most)", "a param is over 256 characters", "the params are over 1024 characters in all" or "params need a template".

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SendChatMessageToAll(KcdMp.Api.ChatMessage,System.String@)
member.summary: to everyone; on a channel, to the players the channel is visible to (a party channel: everyone in a party).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ClearPlayerChat(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: The player's chat forgets every line it holds (the F9 window's mirror is the game's own and stays).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.RegisterChatChannel(System.String,KcdMp.Api.ChatChannelOptions,System.String@)
member.summary: Registers a chat channel: is 1-32 of a-z, 0-9 and _ (upper case is lowered; the default channel "" is always there and cannot be registered). A player types into a channel their chat offers; a line on an unknown channel, one the player cannot see or may not write to is refused with a notice, and a line that passes goes to the players the channel is visible to (see ). Each player is sent the channels they can see, at the join and whenever a channel or their admin or party state changes - not when a function would answer differently: asks again. At most 64 channels; registering a name again replaces it; a reload empties the registry.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.UnregisterChatChannel(System.String)
member.summary: Removes a channel (players' lines on it are refused from then on); false when there is none by that name.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.RefreshChatChannels(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: Sends the channel list again to a player (null = every player): for a channel whose functions answer differently now.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.RegisterCommand(System.String,System.Action{KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String},KcdMp.Api.CommandOptions,System.String@)
member.summary: Registers a chat command: "/name args" runs (the player and the rest of the line, trimmed) before the mode's own and the server's built-ins are asked, so a registered name wins over both. is 1-32 of a-z, 0-9, _ and - (a slash in front and upper case are forgiven); "fight" and "peace" are the server's own and refused. An admin command answers others "Admins only."; a secret one is too. The command is suggested to the players who may use it (AddChatSuggestion), and /help lists it. A handler that throws is caught, logged and counted. At most 256 commands; registering a name again replaces it; a reload empties the registry.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.RegisterCommand(System.String,System.Action{KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String},KcdMp.Api.CommandOptions)
member.summary: RegisterCommand without the reason.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.UnregisterCommand(System.String)
member.summary: Removes a registered command (and its secret mark); false when there is none by that name.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.AddChatSuggestion(System.String,System.String,System.String,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String@)
member.summary: Suggests a command to chats that can suggest (the web chat; the native chat has no such list): for everyone, or for one player. The name is a command name as RegisterCommand takes it, at most 160 characters, the usage that follows the name, at most 96. A suggestion made for a name replaces the server's own and is replaced by a registered command's; a player's own replaces every other. At most 256 for everyone and 64 per player.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.AddChatSuggestion(System.String,System.String,System.String,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: AddChatSuggestion without the reason.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.RemoveChatSuggestion(System.String,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: Takes back a suggestion made with AddChatSuggestion (for everyone, or for the player); false when there is none. A registered command's suggestion and the server's own are not this one's: unregister the command.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.RegisterKeyBinding(System.String,System.String,System.String,System.String@)
member.summary: Declares a key the mode wants (v61): is 1-32 of a-z, 0-9 and _ . : - ; the engine's name for a key ("f2", "insert", "y"; "" = none until the player binds one) - never one of f9, f12, escape, lwin and rwin. Every player is sent the list at the join and on a change and keeps their own choice of key per server; a press comes back as (and a release for every press the mode was told), never while a page, the chat box or the F9 window holds the keyboard. The key is a keyboard key; a player's game also keeps tab, enter, g, t, its walking keys, its push-to-talk key, its third-person key and its chat-scroll keys for itself, so a binding on one of those has no key until the player binds another. At most 32 bindings; registering a name again updates it; a reload empties the registry.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetScoreboardColumns(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{KcdMp.Api.ScoreboardColumnSpec},KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String@)
member.summary: The columns the scoreboard shows besides the game's own (at most 8; ) - for everyone ( null; whoever joins later gets them too) or for one player alone, whose list replaces the world's. A null list takes the columns back (the player's own: to the world's). Each player is sent the columns they may see (an "admin" column only to admins, re-sent when the admin flag changes). The cells are the players' state values () under each key - every client has them, so hiding a column hides nothing of the data. The native board keeps its three columns; the web board draws these.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerHudVisible(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Boolean,System.String@)
member.summary: Shows or hides one of the game's own HUD pieces () on the player's screen: the "hud" component's option of that name, as would set it. False with "no such piece" for another word.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerLoadingHandover(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Object,System.String@)
member.summary: The data the mode hands the web loading screen of a player (its page's loading:handover): one JSON value made of as makes it, at most 16384 bytes. It goes at once, on the channel that reaches the player's game during the level load; call it in . Refused with "no such player", "no data", "too big", "reserved key" or the reason the value has no JSON form.

member.summary: Closes the player's loading screen (a screen that stays until the mode says so - manual_shutdown in ui.toml's [components.loading] - or 240 seconds after the world is ready); on the channel that reaches the game during the level load.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.TimeRatio

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.StoryQuests
member.summary: The game's own story quests in the players' games - off unless a mode turns them on. On, a player's game runs the quests of the level as a single-player game would: a quest can start when a player walks into its place, play its cutscenes, move the player and take their things (the story's people are not there, so most of them cannot be finished). A game decides when it starts, so a change reaches the players who join after it; a game already running keeps what it started with. Set it when the mode starts.

member.summary: The voice chat (v41): how far a voice carries by default, in metres ([voice] range; 0 = off). Setting it tells every client, whose 3D falloff follows it; the server relays nothing beyond it either way.

member.summary: One player's own range in metres (a crier, a whisperer); 0 = the default again.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetVoiceLevels(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{KcdMp.Api.VoiceLevel},System.Int32)
member.summary: v69: the voice levels players switch between with the voice level key (left Ctrl unless they changed it): a whisper, the normal voice, a shout - as many as the mode likes ( at most), in the key's order. Every player speaks at (0-based) from the join; a player already in keeps the level at their place in the list when the new list has one. The level's range becomes the player's own (, which still sets it directly until their next switch). An empty list takes the levels away: the key does nothing and every player's own range goes back to the default.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.VoiceOcclusion
member.summary: v71: how strongly walls muffle the voices: 0 = never, 1 = the default, up to 2. Each player's own game measures what stands between them and every talker they hear (rays, each surface weighted as the game weighs it for its own sounds - stone, plaster, wood, a door, the ground) and muffles that voice; the range itself is unchanged. Setting it tells every client.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.VoiceLevels
member.summary: v69: the voice levels of (empty: none).

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.DefaultVoiceLevel

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.Rain
member.summary: The rain intensity 0..1 every client shows: the weather's own (showers 0.5, drizzle 0.25, storm 1, the rest none) or, once SetRain set a number, that one; SetRain below 0 hands it back to the weather.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.Weather
member.summary: The weather (v22): the level's time-of-day profile every client's sky follows - a preset name (WeatherPresets: "clear", "fair", "cloudy", "overcast", "showers", "drizzle", "storm", "dry_storm") or a profile name as the level's mission file lists it ("cloudless_sunny", "foggy_storm", ...), blended in over the seconds given ([world] weather_blend without them); "" = the server's rotation (a preset every 3 to 5 game hours, the same for every client). The rain is its own lever on top. The property is the profile name; false for a key that is no profile name.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.Entities
member.summary: World entities (plan §6.3): horses and pickups the server owns and every client in range sees. A horse needs a controller — the client that simulates it — from its creation on; a pickup has none. Null when the world is full ([world] max_entities) or the template is empty for an item.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CreateProp(System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Boolean,System.Int32)
member.summary: A prop (v24): a static mesh of the game's object paks placed in the world for everyone in range to see, like a pickup nobody can take - a barrel, a fence, a table, a stone. The mesh is named by the mesh catalogue's id, the file's name without the extension ("barrel_a", when unique) or the path ("objects/manmade/common_furniture/barrels/barrel_a.cgf"; scripting/reference/meshes); without the catalogue only a path passes. scale is uniform (1 = the mesh's own); a rigid prop is a physics body on each client (pushable, its motion not synchronised), a static one stands where it is placed. Null when the mesh resolves to nothing or the world is full. The scale and rigid flag are on IWorldEntity.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CreateInteraction(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.String,System.Single,System.Int32)
member.summary: v79: an interaction point - an invisible spot in the world with a use prompt ("View the house", "Read the notice") shown as written in the game's own use hint while a player looks at it; the use key on it calls OnPlayerInteract. size = the round area to look at, in metres (0.2 - 3, 0.6 by default). An entity of EntityKind.Point (DestroyEntity removes it; a reload removes them all). Null for an empty prompt or a full world.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetEntityPrompt(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String)
member.summary: v79: the use prompt on a prop or an interaction point (an actor's is SetActorPrompt, which this calls for one): the use key on it then calls OnPlayerInteract. null or "" takes a prop's off (a point keeps one: destroy it instead). 48 characters at most, shown as written. False for anything else.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetEntityPrompt(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: v79: the entity's use prompt ("" = none).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CreateActor(System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.String,System.String,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: A server-scripted NPC actor (plan §5.8, v1): a body every client in range shows like a player's remote body - the face and build of `soul` (a name, a soul catalogue id or a GUID of any archetype; "" = the server's appearance pool for `name`), dressed with the clothing / weapon presets (GUIDs, "" = the server's [spawn] presets, like a player, or a peasant's clothes and a sword and shield where those are empty; "none" = none of that kind - an unarmed actor punches, v3), `name` over its head ("" = no label). Nobody controls it: the server's tick walks it towards the MoveActor target at the speed given and the mode hears OnActorArrive. v2 made it hittable, v3 makes it fight back (SetActorHostile). Not yet: its own animations beyond the walk, riding.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CreateAnimal(System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.String,System.Int32)
member.summary: v67: a server-scripted animal - the game's own wolf, boar, deer, hare, sheep, cow, pig, dog ... without its brain, shown by every client in range and walked by the server like an NPC actor (Kind ). `animal` is the kind (the game's class, case-insensitive, spaces allowed: "wolf", "boar", "red deer stag", "RoeDeerHind"; a few plain words too: "deer", "stag", "doe", "cow", "bull", "sheep", "ram", "chicken") or one of its souls (a name, a soul catalogue id or a GUID of an animal archetype - the look). `name` is the mode's name for it (GetEntityName, the log; no label shows over an animal). The actor calls work on it: MoveActor / StopActor / TurnActor, the health, HealActor, SetActorInvulnerable, DestroyEntity; a player's blow or arrow hurts it (OnActorHit, OnActorDeath) and a dead one lies until DestroyEntity. It does not fight back, pose, trade, take a look, wear a label or a torch, get knocked out, robbed or carried (SetActorHostile, SetActorAnim, SetActorPrompt, SetActorLook, SetActorNameplate, SetActorTorch, SetActorKnockedOut, SetActorPocket answer false). Null for an unknown kind, a soul of another archetype, a soul GUID without the tables export (the kind cannot be told), or a full world.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetAnimalHostile(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: 2026-10-07: sets an animal on a player - it runs after them at its kind's pace and bites within its reach every interval (a wolf's or dog's attack on every screen; the bite's damage through the player's armour, the last word). The hunt ends at the player's death, leaving, another world or a long way off (2.5 x the behaviour's radius, 30 m at least), at the animal's death or a MoveActor / StopActor; null calls it off. False for anything but a live animal, or a player not in its world.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetAnimalFlee(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Single)
member.summary: 2026-10-07: runs an animal from a player until it is `distance` metres (3-200) from them; null stops the flight.
