member.summary: 2026-10-07: what an animal does by itself - "calm" (nothing: the default), "aggressive" (hunts a player who comes within `radius` metres), "defensive" (turns on whoever hurts it) or "skittish" (runs from a player within `radius` and from whoever hurts it). False for anything but an animal or an unknown word.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetAnimalBehavior(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: 2026-10-07: the animal's behaviour as names it; "" for anything but an animal.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetAnimalAttack(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: 2026-10-07: a bite's damage (health off an unarmoured player; armour lowers it) and the seconds between bites; 0 = the kind's own.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetAnimalState(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: 2026-10-07: "hunting" and its prey, "fleeing" and the player it runs from, or "calm" and null; ("", null) for anything but an animal.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.MoveActor(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Walks an actor in a straight line to x y z at `speed` metres per second (a walk is ~1.5, a run ~4, a sprint ~6.5 for the clips to match), facing its way; the mode hears OnActorArrive when it gets there. A new target replaces the old one. A z below 0 is "on the ground" there (the server's world data, else the height it walks at). False for anything but an actor.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.StopActor(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: Stops an actor where it is (no OnActorArrive). False for anything but an actor.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetActorAnim(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: A pose on a standing actor: a clip of the game's male animation set by name (the ~7,400 names of Animations/Mannequin/ADB/kcd_male_database.adb, e.g. "behavior_sitting_variation01_loop", "greetings_wave_big_over", "woodchopping_loop_01"; the Lua prelude's ACTOR_ANIM aliases name a few). loop = true plays it until cleared, false once. MoveActor and a death clear it; "" clears it too. The clip travels in the actor's state bag (key "anim"), so a late arrival sees the pose.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.TurnActor(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Single)
member.summary: Turns a standing actor to face `yawDeg` (CryEngine's yaw: 0 = +Y, counter-clockwise). A walking one faces its way.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.MountActor(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Puts an NPC actor on a horse nobody rides or owns: it walks to the horse's left side when it is farther than 2.5 m, climbs on (about 3 s, the game's own mount on every screen) and rides - MoveActor then walks the horse (its pace from the speed: ~1.8 a walk, ~4 a trot, ~7 a canter, ~11 a gallop), StopActor reins in, TurnActor turns it, OnActorArrive tells the end of a ride. instant = true seats it at once. OnActorMount when it sits. False for anything but a standing, unhurt actor not in a fight, or a horse that is dead, ridden, owned or in another world.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.DismountActor(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Takes a mounted actor off its horse (about 3 s, the game's dismount; instant = at once, beside it). OnActorDismount when it stands. False when it rides none.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetActorHorse(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: The horse an actor is on (climbing on, riding or climbing off); null on foot.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsActorMounted(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: Whether the actor sits in the saddle (its climb on done, not climbing off).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.PlayActorVoice(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String,System.String,System.Single)
member.summary: The actor says one of the game's lines by its id (scripting/reference/voice-lines; GetBarkLines lists a bark's), heard from its body by every player within `range` metres (0 = 20, at most 100) with the line's own face. The voice is `voice` when the line was recorded in it, else the actor's own (SetActorVoice, else its soul's), else one of its gender that has it. Returns the line's length in seconds (OnActorVoiceEnd at its end); 0 when it cannot say it (not a live actor, no such line, an export without voices).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.PlayActorBark(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String,System.Single)
member.summary: The actor says a line of one of the game's barks - a plain word ("greeting", "farewell", "self_talk", "work_sigh", "market_call", "pray", "pain" ...) or a pool's own name - picked at random among those its voice recorded. Returns the line's id; "" when none.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.PlayActorConversation(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String,System.Int32,System.Single)
member.summary: Two actors hold one of the game's conversations: its name, or a plain word picked by their genders ("greeting", "farewell", "gossip", "gossip_tavern", "gossip_drunk", "shop_chat", "guard_change", "argument" ...). They turn to each other, a standing one listens between its lines, each line in the speaker's voice with its gesture and face. `sequence` picks one of the conversation's ways through (-1 = at random). Returns the seconds it lasts (OnActorConversationEnd at its end); 0 when it cannot.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.StopActorVoice(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: Cuts what the actor says now on every screen (a conversation ends for both, without its callback). False when it was silent.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsActorSpeaking(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: Whether the actor is saying a line or is in a conversation.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetActorVoice(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: The voice the actor speaks in (the game's voice abbreviation): the mode's, else its soul's; "" = one of its gender per line.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetActorVoice(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String)
member.summary: Gives the actor a voice of the game's (an abbreviation of the voice list, "" = back to its soul's). False for an unknown voice or anything but an actor.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.PlayEntitySound(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Boolean,System.Boolean,System.String@)
member.summary: 2026-10-11: a sound file of the game mode's sounds folder (.ogg, .opus, .wav, .mp3, .flac - its path in the folder: the sounds/ folder next to the mode, or [client] sounds) played at the entity through the game's own sound: positional, in the place's reverb, muffled by walls, on the game's NPC speech bus (the game's master and sound effects volume). Every player within metres who sees the entity hears it; one who comes into range later hears the rest. The file goes only to the players it reaches, the first time it does (from [client] sounds_cdn when the server names one), and starts on their screen when it has arrived - sends it ahead. 0-2; moves an actor's mouth with it. Returns the sound's id ( when it is over; a loop plays until ), 0 and the reason when it cannot.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.StopEntitySounds(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetActorUse(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String)
member.summary: Sends an actor to one of the level's smart objects (GetSmartObjects' key: a bench, a chair, a bed, a well, a weeding bed, a waiting spot ...): it walks to the object, does what the game's NPCs do there (sits down and stays seated, kneels and weeds, leans ...) until StopActorUse or a MoveActor (it gets up first, then walks). OnActorActivity "start" once it is in place, "end" when it got up. One actor per object; false for a taken or unknown object, an activity without a clip for the body, or an actor that is not standing free.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetActorUseAt(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: An activity anywhere (scripting/reference/activities: "sit_ground", "pray_kneel", "lean_wall" ...), with the actor at x y z facing yaw during it (a seat's surface for a seat). The actor walks there first.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.StopActorUse(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Ends the actor's activity or pair: it gets up (immediate = at once, standing, without OnActorActivity). False when it is in none.

member.summary: The actor's activity or pair ("" = none).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetActorUseObject(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: The key of the smart object the actor uses ("" = none, or an activity anywhere).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetSmartObjects(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: The level's smart objects within `radius` metres of x y z (at most 500 m, 256 objects), nearest first; `use` narrows to an activity, a kind ("sit", "lie", "work", "wait", "lean", "pray", "eat", "drink", "talk", "dance", "cheer") or a helper; freeOnly leaves out the ones in use. Empty when the tables export has none for the level (re-export).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.PlayActorPairAnim(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String)
member.summary: Two actors in one of the game's pair animations ("talk", "talk2", "talk_drink", "talk_drunk", "dance", "dance2", "couple_dance", "watch" or the game's name): the second walks to its place facing the first, then both play until StopActorUse on either or a MoveActor. OnActorActivity "start" / "end" for each with the pair's name.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPairAnims
member.summary: The names PlayActorPairAnim takes.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetActorHealth(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Single)
member.summary: v2: an actor's health, 0..100 (a hit takes the model's damage off it, like a player's: the attacker's weapon and the [combat] scale; no armour of its own). Refused on a dead actor (a corpse stays a corpse - DestroyEntity and CreateActor again). 0 kills it now (OnActorDeath, "the world" as the attacker).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.HealActor(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: v4: the actor whole again - full health, every injury gone, the bleeding stopped (HealPlayer for an actor); the body straightens on every screen. Refused on a corpse.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetActorHostile(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v2: the player's client lets the game's lock-on pick the actor's body (on = true) or not; a swing that reaches the actor turns it on by itself, [combat] fight_timeout without a blow, the actor's death and its removal turn it off. An arena mode turns it on before the first blow so the player squares up properly. v3: on = true also makes the player the actor's opponent - it faces them, walks after them and swings ([actors] in server.toml; a blow on the actor does the same by itself with fight_back); false stands it down.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetActorHostileToActor(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Sets an NPC actor on another NPC actor (hostile = true): it faces, chases and swings at it like at a player, and the server lands the blows itself (the weapon of its preset or the fists, x [actors] attack_scale, at most max_damage; OnActorAttackActor may change each). The target fights back once struck with [actors] fight_back, unless it fights someone already. false stands the actor down if it is on that target. False for anything but two living actors in one world.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetActorNameplate(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String)
member.summary: The label over an NPC actor's body on every client: "" = its name again (at most 48 characters).

member.summary: The color of an NPC actor's label, 0xRRGGBBAA; 0 = the default.

member.summary: v45: no blow hurts the actor (a hit on it is refused before OnActorHit); false = it takes hits again.

member.summary: A lit torch in the actor's free hand on every screen (false puts it out) - at peace or in a fight, walking or standing. A death puts it out. False for anything but an NPC actor, or a dead one lit.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsActorTorchLit(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: Whether the actor holds a lit torch (SetActorTorch).

member.summary: 2026-10-10: an actor whose gear holds a bow or a crossbow and its ammo shoots in a fight (on by default): it stands and shoots within metres of its opponent with a clear line, walks closer otherwise, and changes to its melee weapon (when it has one) up close. false = it fights with its melee weapon only. 0..1: how close its arrows fly to where it aims (1 = nearly always on the body). member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsActorButchered(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)

member.summary: 2026-10-03: a stat of the actor's soul, set exactly (0-30) on its body on every screen. The game's own rules on the body answer by it - above all the blows it lands on a player, which the victim's game prices with the attacker's strength (against the weapon's requirement) and combat level. A person's stats: "strength", "agility", "vitality", "speech"; an animal's: "strength", "agility", "vitality", "courage". False for anything but an actor, an unknown name or a level out of range.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetActorSkill(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.String)
member.summary: The level SetActorSkill set; null when the mode never set that skill.

What is Worn dresses and arms its body on every screen in place of its clothing and weapon presets, its armour counts against the blows and arrows on it, its strongest melee weapon prices the blows the server lands for it and is what it drops when it dies (with its first shield). The rest it only carries (GetActorInventory). An actor never given items keeps its presets' dress, their weapon and no armour of record. False for anything but a living server's NPC actor.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetActorInventory(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: 2026-10-03: the actor's items as the mode set them (worn ones marked); null when it was never given any (its presets dress it).

Set before the death or after it: while the body lies dead with anything in it, every screen shows the game's loot prompt on it (OnPlayerLootActor may refuse a search), and what a search takes is the searcher's. An empty list takes the prompt away. False for anything but a server actor or animal.

member.summary: v45: the prompt under the actor's name within reach ("Trade", "Talk"): the player's use key on the actor then reaches the mode as OnActorInteract. "" takes it off (the use key does nothing on it). An actor with a shop shows "Trade" by itself.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CreateEntity(KcdMp.Api.EntityKind,System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Int32)
member.summary: A horse or a pickup; virtualWorld -1 = the controller's world (0 without one), else the world named (v18). A horse's template is its soul: a name, a soul catalogue id or a GUID of the Horse archetype ("" = the server's [spawn] horse_soul); a pickup's is its item class (a name, an item catalogue id or a GUID). v67: makes an NPC actor - the template is its soul, the rest as with no name and the default clothing and weapons (the controller is ignored; -1 = the shared world); an animal - the template as 's `animal`.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.DestroyEntity(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: Removes an entity from the world, for everyone (a horse under a rider dismounts them). False when there is no such entity. v62: a horse in a running pull-down (IPlayer.IsInPullDown) is not removed at once - the game's pair is playing on it on the players' screens: it is destroyed when the pull-down ends, about 6.5 s after it started, and this returns true meanwhile with the horse still there.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetEntityPos(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Nullable{System.Single})
member.summary: Moves an entity; its controller (if any) puts the real thing there. A ridden horse takes its rider along.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetEntityController(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: Hands the simulation of an entity to a player (null = nobody: it stands still until someone takes it) — the way a horse changes hands. Refused (false) while someone else rides it. v62: a horse in a running pull-down (IPlayer.IsInPullDown) keeps its controller until the pull-down ends, about 6.5 s after it started: this returns true and the hand-over is done then - unless the new controller has left by then or the horse has another rider - and an order for the player who controls it meanwhile cancels the one waiting.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.MountPlayer(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: Puts a player in the saddle of a horse: control goes to them and their client mounts it (the horse may be anywhere; the game walks or teleports the player onto it). False when it is not a horse, someone else rides it, the player is not in the world, is in a pull-down (IPlayer.IsInPullDown) or is knocked out (IPlayer.IsKnockedOut) - or the horse is part of a running pull-down and not already theirs to control (it cannot change hands until it ends). A player who carries or is carried is mounted and the carry ends ("mounted").

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetHorseOwner(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: v53: who owns the horse from now on (null = nobody): their horse in the game (its saddlebags in their inventory, the game's plain "Mount"), the bags theirs whoever simulates it; anyone else mounts it as a thief (IGameMode.OnPlayerStealHorse). A horse made for a player (CreateEntity with a controller) is theirs from the start. A player may own several.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPlayerHorses(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: v53: every horse in the world the player owns.

False when it is not a horse.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetHorseGear(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: v53: what the horse wears - saddle, bridle, saddlebags, caparison - as item class GUIDs; null = not a horse.

member.summary: v53: the horse dressed in exactly this gear (classes by any catalogue key) on every screen. False when it is not a horse.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetHorseHealth(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity)
member.summary: v73: a horse's health, 0..100 (100 when it is made; also ). A player's blow or arrow takes the model's damage off it (the attacker's weapon and the [combat] scale, no armour of its own, a third of a blow on a person's body wherever it lands - about 8 short-sword slashes; IGameMode.OnHorseHit may change it) - not on the horse they ride, and on another player's horse (its rider's, else its owner's) only where they could hit that player (pvp, teams, parties). At 0 it dies on every screen (IGameMode.OnHorseDeath): its rider is thrown off, nobody mounts it any more and the body is removed a minute later. -1 for anything but a horse.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetHorseHealth(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Single)
member.summary: v73: sets a living horse's health (0..100); 0 kills it now (IGameMode.OnHorseDeath with no attacker). Raising it heals the horse. False for a dead horse (it stays dead until it is removed) or anything but a horse.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetHorseInvulnerable(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v73: no blow hurts the horse (a hit on it is refused before IGameMode.OnHorseHit); false = it takes hits again. False for anything but a horse.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPlayerMount(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: The horse the player rides, or null.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ThrowPlayerFromHorse(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean,System.String@)
member.summary: v62: has the player's game throw them off the horse they ride - the fall everyone else sees too (IGameMode.OnPlayerThrown follows once it happened). asks for the game's strong throw, the one a rearing horse gives. The throw is the rider's own game's to play, so it may decline: false, with the reason as the asker reads it, when the player is not in the world, dead, not on a horse, already falling or being pulled off it (IPlayer.IsInPullDown), cannot be thrown by the rules (SetPlayerRiderThrow), or their game cannot (an older or unsupported build). True means the order went out - the throw itself comes a moment later, or does not come at all if their game refuses it; a mode that has to know waits for OnPlayerThrown.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerRiderHeadHit(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v62: whether a head hit on a branch or a beam throws the rider (the game's own rule, on unless a mode turns it off for the player). A rider who meets the obstacle passes under it; other throws are not affected (SetPlayerRiderThrow). Lasts until changed or the player leaves, through respawns.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerRiderThrow(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v62: whether the throws take the rider off the horse - a head hit, the horse, ThrowPlayerFromHorse (on unless a mode turns them off for the player). Off, none of those throws them. A pull-down is not a throw: it has its own switch (SetPlayerPullDown) and its own veto (IGameMode.OnPlayerPullDown, per rider), and neither it nor PullPlayerFromHorse reads this setting. Lasts until changed or the player leaves, through respawns.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerPullDown(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v62: whether the player may pull riders off their horses - the game's own take-down, the "Pull down" prompt on a rider's body for a player on foot; off by default for everyone (a mode that wants it switches it on, usually at the spawn). It is sent to their game on every change and with every spawn, and the server refuses the ask of a player without it. The rest is the server's and the mode's: the weapon's reach and the horse's pace (the game's numbers plus 1.5 m and 1 m/s), pvp, teams and parties, a wall between the two, then IGameMode.OnPlayerPullDown's veto and chance. Lasts until changed or the player leaves, through respawns.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.PullPlayerFromHorse(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean,System.String@)
member.summary: v62: pulls off the horse they ride, with on foot beside it doing the game's take-down - the mode's own order, which skips the weapon, reach, pace, wall, policy and right checks, the rider's SetPlayerRiderThrow rule and the mode's OnPlayerPullDown. false plays the failed pair (the rider stays in the saddle). The pair plays on the two games and everyone who sees both; IGameMode.OnPlayerPulledDown tells the outcome. False with the reason when the victim is not riding, either is not standing in the world, busy (a pull-down, a fall, a cart, flight, dice, a shop or a dialogue), the two are more than about 6 m apart, cannot see each other yet, or the puller's game cannot play the pair.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetCarrying(System.Boolean,KcdMp.Api.CarryRules)
member.summary: v62: switches the players' own grab on or off, with its rules (null = the defaults). On, the game's "grab" prompt shows on a body that lies down (a dead character's, a knocked-out player's or actor's, as / / allow) and a player's ask is checked (the body in his view and within reach, in the open when [validation] line_of_sight is on, free, the mode's IGameMode.OnPlayerCarry). Off by default; the mode's own orders do not need it. A carry in progress goes on when it is switched off. A mode reload switches it off again with the rules reset (and every body carryable): the new mode's init sets what it wants. Writes the world state key "carry" ("1" while on): do not set that key yourself.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetCarrying
member.summary: v62: whether the players' own grab is on, and its rules (the defaults until SetCarrying gave others).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CarryPlayer(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Single,System.String@)
member.summary: v62: carries : the carrier's game plays the grab and the carry, the target's game is carried by the carrier's body, and every screen with both bodies sees it. The target need not be knocked out - they show knocked out for the carry and wake after it, unless the mode knocked them out (SetPlayerKnockedOut). is the carrier's pace in metres per second (0 = the rules' of SetCarrying, 2.4 by default; at most 4). It works with SetCarrying off. False with the reason when either is not standing in the world in one virtual world, busy (riding, in a cart, flying, dice, a pull-down or fall, already carrying or carried, a fight for the carrier), more than 6 m apart, cannot see each other yet, or a game cannot take part. IGameMode.OnPlayerCarryStart follows.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.StopCarry(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v62: has the carry of (either the carrier or the carried player) put down: the carrier's game plays the put and the body lies at (x, y, z) facing yawDeg when the position is given (else where the game puts it), IGameMode.OnPlayerCarryEnd follows with "mode". A put ordered while the grab still goes on waits for it to finish. ends it now, with no put animation. False when is neither carrying nor carried. Either party is accepted, so which of them may order it is the mode's to decide: a command that lets players put down what they carry checks IPlayer.IsCarrying first, or the carried player ends his own carry by typing it.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerKnockedOut(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Boolean,System.Single,System.String@)
member.summary: v62: knocks the player out () or wakes them: the game's own knock-out - they drop, their screen goes dark, everyone sees the body lying - with their health as it is. A knocked-out player cannot fight, ride, act, make an emote or start a dice match, and can be carried. > 0 wakes them by itself after that long, 0 keeps them down until the mode wakes them (or they die, leave or respawn). False with the reason when they are not in the world, dead, riding, in a cart, flying, in a dice match or a pull-down or fall. A game of an older or unsupported build is knocked out all the same (the server holds the player down; that game just does not show it). Knocking out one who is out already sets the timer anew. A carrier is made to put down.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.HitchHorse(KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,KcdMp.Api.IWorldEntity,System.Int32)
member.summary: 2026-10-10: a horse (CreateHorse, a player's own) put in front of the cart in slot `slot` (1 = "horse1", 2 = "horse2" on a wagon; 0 = the first without a player's horse in it, an empty one first). Nobody sees the horse as itself any more - the cart draws it in the slot with its coat - and it pulls as its type and strength say (SetHorseType, SetHorseStat); it keeps its owner, stats and saddlebags, goes where the cart goes, and nobody may mount it, walk it or turn it until UnhitchHorse. False when the cart or the horse is none, the slot is taken by a player's horse or none, or the horse is ridden (a player or an actor), dead, in front of another cart or in another world.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.CreateSiegeEngine(System.String,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32)
member.summary: v77: a siege engine at (x, y, z) facing yawDeg - where it throws: "trebuchet" (the game's trebuchet, throwing a stone 100-330 m) or "cannon" (the game's bombard, a ball up to ~400 m). z below 0 = on the ground there, which needs the level's heightmap or navmesh on the server (the shots leave from the engine's height). A player takes the operator's place with the use key at it, aims (the right mouse button held, looking), loads and fires; the mode may do it all itself (AimSiegeEngine, LoadSiegeEngine, FireSiegeEngine). "ladder" is a siege ladder (the game's 10 m one, climbed with the game's own climb): (x, y, z) is its foot and yawDeg the way it leans - toward the wall, its top 2 m out and 9.5 m up; it stands against the wall until a player at its top knocks it down (PushSiegeLadder), and a player at its foot raises it again (RaiseSiegeLadder). "stones" is a pile of hurling stones (nine, on a wall walk - give the walk's height): a player beside it lifts one with the use key, throws it where they look, or puts it back. virtualWorld -1 = the shared world. Null for an unknown kind, a full world or a ground it cannot find. DestroyEntity removes it.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPlayerWeight(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: v62: the server's own estimate of what the player carries, what they may carry and whether that is too much (see ) - a figure the carry-weight check works from, worked out from the item records and the strength, perks, potions and drinks the server knows of (worn items count, as in the game), never from what the player's game says it carries. Nothing is ever taken from a heavy player: a player over the limit is only slower in the game, and the check watches whether they move as the game forbids. is false while the server cannot tell (before the player's first whole progress report, without the tables export's item catalogue, while their bag is not being followed): the other fields are then 0 and false; so for a player who is not connected.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPlayerProgressAudit(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: v62: this session's counters of the progression check for the player - the rises it could not explain, the ones it put back (or logged that it would, in observe) and the ones the mode vouched for, the rewrites, probes and stale reports, and what the player's game said about its XP counting and its first session (see ); for a mode's own rules and a status page. For a player who is not connected it is all zeros.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerProgress(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.ProgressSnapshot)
member.summary: A whole restore: every stat and skill in the snapshot set exactly (), the perks made exactly its list when it carries one (perks the soul holds beyond the list are taken away once the server has heard the game's own list), the nourishment and energy put on the soul. Every stat and skill gets its perk points set in the same order, exactly as says - 0 included, so points the fresh character had do not outlive the restore (the Warfare entry sets its points alone: its level follows the weapon skills). The snapshot's mainlevel entry sets the pool of perk points that belongs to no stat or skill; its level is ignored (the game derives it). A name the server does not know is skipped and logged. False for a null snapshot.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPlayerOutfits(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerOutfits(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.PlayerOutfits)
member.summary: v82: a restore of the player's three outfits, for after the bag's restore (): the player's game dresses again out of what the player carries - a class they no longer carry is left out - and each other outfit the first time the player switches to it; until then its reports carry those as set, so a logout without opening them keeps them. A set made before the player is in the world goes out right after their spawn. Reports the game sent before it applied the set are dropped, so the fresh game's empty outfits never overwrite it. False for a list that is not three outfits, a current outfit outside 0..2, an outfit over 64 items or an empty class.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GetPlayerDiscovery(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String)
member.summary: The player's discovery record for (the server's level when null): a block per kind the server holds, the reading block (global) whatever the level, the kinds the player's game can do. The blocks are canonical typed bytes, ready to save as they are. Never null for a player who exists - a kind not yet reported or set is absent from it. Right after it answers what was set.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.SetPlayerDiscovery(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.DiscoverySnapshot,System.Boolean)
member.summary: A restore (or any set): the blocks of the snapshot taken into the record at once and sent to the player's game - the ones made before the player is in the world right after their spawn, in order. With false (the default) every block is united with what the record and the game already hold: discovery only grows, so a restore can never take away what the player found since they joined. True makes the record exactly the snapshot's for the kinds it holds, and the game forgets the rest of them first (the books and the map pin; not the places yet). A block of another level than the server's is kept in the record and not sent. A block the server cannot read (an unknown format, bytes that are no well-formed block) is skipped and logged and the call returns false; the rest are applied. No callback follows a set of the mode's own.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ForgetPlayerDiscovery(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.DiscoveryKinds)
member.summary: The player has found nothing of these kinds again: the record emptied and the game told to forget (a mode that lets one game switch between characters calls it at every switch). is every kind; asking for one the game cannot forget (the places, today) - by name or through All - forgets the others and returns false: the places stay in the record and in the game, so a mode that switches characters in one game must not keep the places (leave them out of ) until they can be forgotten.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.IsPlayerDiscoveryKnown(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.DiscoveryKinds)
member.summary: Whether the record of these kinds is the game's own: a whole report of each has arrived, or the mode set it. A mode that saves on a timer waits for it, so a record that is still empty because the game has not reported is never saved over a character's own.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.GivePlayerBuff(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.String,System.Single)
member.summary: The buffs (v21): the game's own timed or permanent modifiers on a soul (a potion's effect, an injury, drunkenness; Libs/Tables/rpg/buff*.xml, published as scripting/reference/buffs), given and taken by the server. A buff is named by the game's name (well_rested, case-insensitive), the buff catalogue's id or its GUID (without the export only GUIDs, unchecked). The player's client adds the game's buff once and removes it by GUID; the record lives until RemovePlayerBuff, the given seconds (0 = none), HealPlayer or the respawn - the game's own duration may end a timed buff's visible effect earlier. False when the key resolves to nothing or the player is not in the world.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ClaimedBuffClasses
member.summary: The buff classes the server takes over (the claim; [combat] claimed_buffs at start): every client undoes the game's own application of any buff of those classes unless the server gave it, so a local potion, poison or drunkenness opens no hole against the server-owned vitals. Class names as the catalogue lists them ("Potion", "Poison", "Alcohol", ...); an unknown one is logged and ignored; an empty set claims nothing. The whole list goes to every client.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.StartFight(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: Puts the two players in a fight: from then on either one's client lets the game's lock-on pick the other's body (the direction indicators, combat mode). The server starts one by itself when a swing reaches a body and on /fight; a fight ends after [combat] fight_timeout seconds without a blow (calling this on a running fight restarts that clock), on a death, /peace, a disconnect or EndFight. False when it cannot start (pvp off, a player not standing in the world).

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.StartDiceMatch(KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer,System.Single,System.Int32,System.String@,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Starts a match of the game's own dice game between two players standing together at a dice table: both games walk their player to the table and seat the other across it (a stand-in with their look), the server deals every throw, and the challenger throws first. The stake - `bet` Groschen from each player, 0 for none - leaves both purses now and goes to the winner at the end (both get it back when the match is called off). `gameType` is the game's own type of game, which sets the goal: 0 beggar (1500 points), 1 wagoner (2000), 5 craftsman (3000), 9 courtier (4000) - the ones played without badges. The mode sets the match's rules: `turnTimeout` is how many seconds a player may take for one move before losing the match (5 to 3600), `range` how far apart in metres the two may stand when it starts (0.5 to 8; the games look for the dice table nearest the challenger). Null, with the reason as the player reads it, when it cannot start ("Hans is too far away - stand together at a dice table.", "Henry cannot cover the bet of 50 Groschen." ...): a player not in the world, dead, on horseback, in a fight, in a shop, knocked out, carrying or carried, or already playing, the two farther apart than `range`, or short of the stake - or, for the mode, a game type with badges or a rule out of its bounds.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.EndDiceMatch(KcdMp.Api.IDiceMatch,KcdMp.Api.IPlayer)
member.summary: Ends a running match: `winner` (one of its two players) takes the stakes, null calls it off (both get theirs back). Both games end too. OnDiceMatchEnd hears it with the reason "the mode". False when the match is over already.

member.name: M:KcdMp.Api.IServerApi.ImportMap(System.String,System.Boolean)
member.summary: v83: an export (exports/<name>.zip) into the map. member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.Look
member.summary: v51: the look of a human body - the parts of the game's characters (Libs/Tables/Character/CharacterComponent.xml, through the tables export's "looks" rows) it wears in place of its soul's own: Body = the skin (the torso, arms, hands, legs and feet), Head = the face, Hair = the hair and its colour, Beard = the beard. "" = the soul's own part. is the one-line form a database keeps - "body=m_body_tan_02;head=m_head_004;hair=m_hair_005_blonde;beard=m_beard_03", the empty parts left out, "" for none - and reads it back (the Lua API's LookToString / LookFromString are the same form). v54: Gender - "" a man's body (the default), "female" a woman's: the female skeleton with a woman's soul, and every part a woman's (a woman has no beard). A look whose parts are all a woman's is a woman's without saying so; "female" with no part at all is a woman with her soul's own face, hair and skin. The one-line form carries it as "gender=female".

A look whose parts are all a woman's is a woman's without saying so; "female" with no part at all is a woman with her soul's own face, hair and skin. The one-line form carries it as "gender=female".

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.IShop
member.summary: A shop a game mode keeps on the server (v45): a title, the items it sells with a price and a stock, whether it buys from the players and at what fraction of the catalogue price, and its purse. A player sees it on the shop screen (, or the use key on an NPC actor the shop was put on with ) and buys and sells on it; every transaction passes through / , the money and the items move by the server's own GiveItem, so the inventory audit explains them. Prices are Groschen; the wire carries tenths.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.MapObjectSpec
member.summary: v80: an object to place on the level's map, or what to make an object into (IServerApi.CreateMapObject, SetMapObject). Mesh is one of the game's own meshes ("objects/manmade/....cgf" - the reference's meshes list); X, Y, Z in metres; YawDeg turns it about the up axis as a player's yaw does (0 = facing +Y), PitchDeg tips its front up, RollDeg leans it sideways (applied roll first, then pitch, then yaw); Scale is uniform (0.05-20), or with ScaleY / ScaleZ the X of a stretched mesh. Material swaps the mesh's own for one of the game's ("" = its own), Tint colours it 0xRRGGBBAA (0 = none); Solid makes players and the server's collision meet it; ViewDistance is the engine's view distance ratio (0 = by its size); Layer is the map layer it belongs to ("base" unless named - a new name makes the layer, switched on); Group is a folder for the editor. Persist false keeps it for this run of the game mode only: never saved, gone at a restart and when the mode is reloaded (its OnGameModeInit makes it again) - true writes it into the server's map like an admin's.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.MapObjectSpec.ScaleY
member.summary: Phase 7: stretched - the scale along the mesh's own Y and Z (Scale is then its X one, each 0.05-20); 0 = Scale. Meshes only.

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.MapObjectSpec.Params
member.summary: v83: an entity's settings, Mesh being one of the game's working things in place of a mesh - "entity:light" ("r g b radius strength style": the colour 0..1, metres, a multiplier, the game's light style 0 = steady), "entity:effect" ("name [scale]": a particle effect, "WH_Particels.fires.candle"), "entity:sound" ("trigger": an audio trigger, "a_l_hot_wood_loop"), "entity:marker" ("tag": a place only the editor and the mode know - a spawn point), "entity:door" ("model [locked]": one of the game's doors, "objects/characters/assets/doors/....cdf"). A door's key in the door functions (SetDoorState, SetDoorCheck ...) is "KcdMp_map_" + its id; it takes no use prompt (the game's own open and close).

member.name: P:KcdMp.Api.MapObjectSpec.Attach
member.summary: Phase 7: the map object this one sits on (0 = none) - it moves, turns and stretches with that one and goes when that one is deleted. A board on a wall, a lamp on a cart.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.MapPictureInfo
member.summary: Phase 7, boards: Mesh "picture:<name>" shows one of the map's pictures (a PNG in the map folder's pictures/, GetMapPictures), "surface:<page>" a web surface page of the interface (ui.toml [surfaces.<page>]; the map's own surface entity - GetMapObjectSurface - talks to it like any). A board is 1 m wide (Scale) and as tall as its picture or page is for that width (ScaleZ stretches it), its face looking where YawDeg turns +Y; Params says how its see-through parts show - "solid", "blend" (soft) or "cutout" (hard) - and its glow 0-1 ("cutout 0.3"; "" on a new picture board = "blend" when the picture has see-through pixels, else "solid"); Use is a picture's prompt (OnPlayerUseMapObject) or a surface's (OnPlayerUseWebSurface). Boards are never solid.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.PocketRules
member.summary: The rules of pickpocketing (IServerApi.SetPickpocketing): what the game's "Rob" on a body may take, from whom, how often and how close. A number that is not usable (below zero, not a number) is the default.
member.param: metres the thief may stand from the body when he reaches for its pockets (default 3, at most 6); the game's own reach is about 2.4 m, the server allows for the positions being a few frames old.
seconds before the same thief may rob the same victim again, counted from the start (default 30; 0 = none).
stacks the pockets offer at most (default 8, never more than 11 - the game's wheel has no more places).
the most of one class the pockets offer (default 5, at most 9999): a non-stacking class shows one tile per item.
the thief must stand behind the victim, within 70 degrees of straight behind (default false: the game's own roll already punishes the front).
the shortest a session may take before it may take anything (default 2.5, at most 60): a claim sooner is refused.
a player's purse is in the pockets, as one entry (default false).
the share of the purse that entry holds (0..1, default 0.1).
the most that entry holds, in Groschen (default 100, at most 6553.5).
an NPC actor with pockets (IServerApi.SetActorPocket) can be robbed (default true).
item classes, item names or catalogue categories that are never offered (the game's own quick-slot containers, aliases, NPC tools and key rings are never offered whatever this says).

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.PlayerOutfits
member.summary: v82: a player's three outfits - the game's own outfits, the inventory's flags A, B and C - each as the item classes it wears. The game keeps an outfit as the item instances it wears and a join makes every item anew, so without a record only the outfit the bag's restore dressed comes back after a join. The server keeps what the player's game last reported (, ); a mode saves that with the character and hands it back after the next join (, after the bag's restore): the player's game then dresses each outfit again out of what the player carries - a class they no longer carry is left out - the current one last.
member.param: The outfit the player wears: 0 (A), 1 (B) or 2 (C).
Three lists of item class GUIDs, one entry per item (a class twice for two of it), at most 64 each. An outfit the player never put together is an empty list.

A dictionary's keys may be any spelling of the name the server knows (warfare for fencing); the snapshot returns holds the canonical ones.

The soul's energy (the Rest); null = unknown / leave it.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.SceneryHit
member.summary: v93: a player's melee blow on the level, as their own game struck it (IGameMode.OnPlayerHitScenery) - named the way a client script's GetLookTarget names a look. X, Y, Z the point struck (metres); NormalX/Y/Z which way the surface faces there; Surface the game's surface type ("mat_wood", "mat_rock" ...). A tree, a bush or a piece of scenery comes with Mesh (the model, lower case - its folder tells an oak from a pine) and its world box (MinX..MaxZ; Center* its middle): the mesh and the centre name one tree for the whole server and are what IServerApi.RemoveLevelObject takes. Mesh is "" when the game cannot tell which piece was struck. An Object comes with its level Name (a door's or a chest's key) and Class. Weapon is the drawn weapon by its table name as the server knows it, "fists" without one.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.SiegeEngineInfo
member.summary: v77: a siege engine as it stands (IServerApi.GetSiegeEngineInfo). Phase is "rest", "winding" (a trebuchet's arm going down), "cocked", "loading", "loaded", "firing" or "destroyed" - a siege ladder's "up", "falling", "down", "raising" or "destroyed" (it has no operator, aim or shots) - a pile of stones' "rest", "lifting", "holding" or "throwing" (Operator: the player with its stone in their hands; Shots: the stones on it, Aim: the last throw's point); Aim is the point it is aimed at (null = never aimed: it throws straight ahead); Pitch and Speed are the throw the aim asks for (degrees, m/s) and Range the throw's reach on level ground; InReach is false when the aim lies beyond its limits (it throws as far or as high as it can). Health is the structure in percent (-1 = it cannot be destroyed); Shots the shots left (-1 = no limit); Fired how many it fired; SecondsLeft the running phase's time (null = none runs).

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.SiegeRules
member.summary: v77: one engine's own rules (SetSiegeEngineRules); null leaves the kind's own. The cycle's seconds (WindSeconds - a trebuchet's winding, LoadSeconds, FireSeconds - the whole firing, the arm settling or the smoke clearing; never shorter than the release), its reach on level ground in metres (MinRange / MaxRange - a trebuchet throws anywhere between, a cannon's MaxRange is its charge at the highest wedge), TurnRate (degrees a second) and Traverse (degrees either way from where it stands now; 180 = all round, 0 = it throws only where it faces), the impact (Damage at the point - a player's health is 100 -, Radius and FullRadius in metres, StructureDamage - the percent of another engine's structure a hit at the point takes), OperateRange (how near its operator stands) and Crew (a trebuchet: how many of its two winch places a player's winding needs manned - 2 by default, 0 = its operator winds it alone). A siege ladder takes FallSeconds (its fall once knocked down), RaiseSeconds (standing it up again), Damage (what a climber at its very top takes from the fall - less the lower they were; a quarter of it whoever it lands on), OperateRange (how near its top a player knocks it down, how near its foot one raises it) and PolearmToPush (whether a player needs a polearm to knock it down - true by default). A pile of stones takes Capacity (the stones a full pile holds), RefillSeconds (how long a thrown stone takes to come back; 0 = never), Damage, Radius and FullRadius (a stone's blow) and OperateRange (how near the pile a player lifts a stone); the rest is the engines'.

member.name: T:KcdMp.Api.ThirdPersonMode
member.summary: v62: the third-person view a game mode gives a player (): the game's own chase camera behind the player instead of their eyes. The game's camera still takes over where it always does - a dialogue, a menu, a minigame; riding a horse keeps the view, and so do fighting and aiming a bow, a crossbow or a gun unless the mode asks for first person there (the two flags of ).

member.name: F:KcdMp.Api.ThirdPersonMode.Allow

member.name: F:KcdMp.Api.ThirdPersonMode.Force
